title: A Orchard for the Vow Again
premise: Edmund Thornbury, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended at the altar, has stopped believing in the ceremonies he sells. When his estranged family summons him to a reunion at their crumbling orchard estate, he hires Marisol Vega—a ferry mechanic with a sharp tongue and a rented tuxedo—to pose as his partner for one weekend. But the fake date curdles into something real by dessert, and when a storm cancels the last ferry of the season, Marisol is stranded in Edmund's world. To keep her, Edmund must finally claim the inheritance he's been running from: not the orchard, but the family—and the love—he swore he'd never trust again.
about_author: Hazel Delacroix writes romance from a converted apple barn on the coast, where she keeps a notebook of overheard vows from strangers on ferries. A former event planner herself, she believes every love story deserves a second seating.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Before the Frost
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Burned out and bitter, Edmund books passage home to Thornbury Orchard for a reunion he dreads, planning to announce he's selling his share. At the dock he meets Marisol, fixing the very ferry he's boarding, and impulsively offers her money to be his date. The beat: reluctant hope disguised as a business transaction.

chapters.title: Cider, Lies, and Grandmother's Roses
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The fake couple performs through orchard tours and a tense family dinner, but Marisol's easy warmth cracks Edmund's armor—and his grandmother sees straight through them both, saying nothing. By dessert, their staged affection has become indistinguishable from the real thing. The beat: the lie turning sweet and dangerous.

chapters.title: Storm Warning at Thornbury Gate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Marisol discovers the payment envelope and feels used just as a storm rolls in; they fight in the rain among the apple trees, truths spilling—his abandoned wedding, her fear of being anyone's arrangement. The last ferry is cancelled, stranding her. The beat: climax, where pretense shatters and raw want remains.

chapters.title: What Stays After the Season Ends
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Morning after the storm: Edmund publicly withdraws the sale, claiming his place in the family and asking Marisol to stay—not as a date, but as himself, unscripted. She misses the first ferry of spring on purpose, staying through winter in the orchard cottage. The beat: resolution, inheritance redefined as belonging.
